decisions.reason: A perfect binder fits squarely within the firm's long-standing knowledge of print finishing equipment, so the firm can interpret customer feedback and service the product with its existing expertise, which favours keeping it despite the missing website evidence for 2020-2021.

The fully automatic perfect binder extends the same binding know-how the firm already holds, and although its higher complexity and the pandemic-hit print market add some risk, the related knowledge base supports retaining it.

The inline/nearline booklet maker builds on the firm's established finishing portfolio and its supplier relationships, so the firm can absorb and apply the needed knowledge, though integration with customers' printing systems makes it slightly riskier.
